backlog.spec: Ramp the Muon momentum from 0.85 at step 0 to 0.95 linearly over the first 300 optimizer steps, then hold at 0.95. Implement by setting the momentum value of the Muon param group each step from the step counter. Leave all other optimizer settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz orthogonalization iterations inside Muon from 5 to 3 to save wall-clock time per step, which matters under the fixed 300 s budget. Keep the quintic coefficients consistent with the reduced iteration count (use the same coefficient set, just fewer loops). Everything else stays the same.
backlog.title: Fewer Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS for the embedding, lm_head, and per-layer scalar Adam groups from (0.8, 0.95) to (0.9, 0.95), keeping the same LR values. Muon's own momentum is not affected. This tests whether a smoother first-moment estimate helps the non-matrix parameters.
backlog.title: Adam beta1 0.9 for embeddings and scalars

backlog.spec: Scale the Muon weight decay by a linear schedule that starts at WEIGHT_DECAY and decays to 0 at the end of training, using the same time-fraction variable that drives the LR schedule. Apply the factor each step to the decay term only. The incumbent keeps decay constant.
backlog.title: Decoupled weight decay decays to zero

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO from 0.0 to 0.03 so the LR ramps linearly from zero over the first 3% of the time budget before the warmdown begins. This is a stability guard for the high EMBEDDING_LR of 0.6 and SCALAR_LR of 0.5 during the first few hundred steps.
backlog.title: Longer LR warmup

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR schedule with a cosine decay that goes from full LR at the start of the warmdown phase (WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget before the end) to FINAL_LR_FRAC at the end. Keep WARMDOWN_RATIO at 0.5. Apply the same multiplier to all parameter groups.
backlog.title: Cosine warmdown instead of linear

backlog.spec: Use a warmdown multiplier of sqrt(remaining_fraction) during the final WARMDOWN_RATIO of training, where remaining_fraction goes from 1 to 0 across that phase. This decays the LR more slowly at first and faster near the end than linear. Apply to all groups.
backlog.title: Sqrt-shaped warmdown

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC from 0.0 to 0.05 so the LR does not decay fully to zero at the end of the time budget. The warmdown still spans WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget. This keeps some gradient signal in the last steps.
backlog.title: Nonzero final LR fraction

backlog.spec: Before each optimizer step, clip the global gradient norm of all trainable parameters to 1.0 using torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_. This guards against occasional spikes at the high learning rates used for the Adam groups. No other changes.
backlog.title: Gradient norm clipping

backlog.spec: Apply a soft cap to the output logits before the cross-entropy: logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15). Apply it only in the forward path used for training and for validation so the harness evaluation of the same model is consistent. Keep lm_head unchanged otherwise.
backlog.title: Logit soft-capping

backlog.spec: Apply RMSNorm (without learned gain, or with a learned per-head gain initialized to one) to the query and key vectors per head after the rotary embedding is applied, before the scaled dot product. This stabilizes attention logits at the chosen learning rates. Keep the rest of the attention block unchanged.
backlog.title: QK normalization

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with squared ReLU: x = relu(W_in x) and then x = x * x before the output projection. Keep the 4x hidden expansion and the bias-free linear layers as in the incumbent. This is a cheap nonlinearity with strong results in small GPTs.
backlog.title: Squared-ReLU MLP

backlog.spec: Change each transformer block from sequential attention then MLP to parallel form: x = x + attn(norm(x)) + mlp(norm(x)), using one shared pre-norm for both branches. Keep residual scalars and the rest unchanged. This reduces the sequential depth per step and may speed up training.
backlog.title: Parallel attention and MLP blocks

backlog.spec: Pass the value projection of the first layer forward and mix it into every later layer's values with a learned per-layer scalar initialized to 0.5. Specifically, v_l = a_l * v_l + (1 - a_l) * v_0 for layers after the first. Adds only a few scalar parameters.
backlog.title: Value residual from first layer

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 6 and keep ASPECT_RATIO at 64 so model_dim is adjusted accordingly, trading layers for width. Fewer layers run faster per step, which can yield more optimizer steps in 300 s. Keep HEAD_DIM and all other hyperparameters the same.
backlog.title: Shallower and wider model

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH from 8 to 10 and reduce ASPECT_RATIO from 64 to 52 so model_dim stays close to the incumbent's cost, favoring depth over width. Keep HEAD_DIM at 128 so the head count adjusts. Check that DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 still fits in 40 GB.
backlog.title: Deeper and narrower model

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM from 128 to 64, which doubles the number of attention heads at the same model_dim. More heads with smaller dimension can capture more diverse attention patterns in a small model. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Smaller head dimension

backlog.spec: Change WINDOW_PATTERN from 'SSSL' to 'SSLL' so two of the four layers in each group use full context. Full attention is more expensive but may help a 300 s model that sees short training. Keep all other settings.
backlog.title: Window pattern with more full-context layers

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base frequency from 10000 to 100000 to stretch the positional wavelengths. This is a one-constant change in the rotary embedding setup. Keep the rest of the attention block unchanged.
backlog.title: Higher RoPE base

backlog.spec: Reduce TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**18 so each optimizer step has half as many tokens and the 300 s budget yields about twice as many updates. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 and adjust gradient accumulation so the micro-batch math remains correct. Learning rates stay the same.
backlog.title: Smaller total batch for more steps

backlog.spec: Increase TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE from 2**19 to 2**20 so each step averages more tokens and gradients are less noisy. Keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE at 64 and increase gradient accumulation steps to match. Learning rates stay the same. This tests whether a bigger batch helps at fixed wall-clock time.
backlog.title: Larger total batch

backlog.spec: Start training with a total batch of 2**17 tokens and double it at fixed fractions of the time budget (for example at 25% and 60%) until reaching 2**19 tokens. Recompute gradient accumulation per phase. Keep learning rates unchanged. Smaller early batches give faster early progress.
backlog.title: Batch size ramp-up

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss of 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training cross-entropy to keep the output logit scale stable. Do not add it to the validation loss path. This is a light regularizer on the unembedding.
backlog.title: Z-loss on logits

backlog.spec: Add dropout with probability 0.05 on the attention output and on the MLP output of each block, active only during training. Turn it off in eval mode. Keep all learning rates unchanged. This is a light regularizer test for overfitting under repeated data.
backlog.title: Dropout in attention and MLP

backlog.spec: During training, skip each transformer block's residual branch with probability 0.05 (stochastic depth), scaling the surviving branch output by 1/(1-p). Disable this in evaluation. Keep the rest of the code unchanged.
backlog.title: Layer drop during training

backlog.spec: Initialize the output projection of the attention block and of the MLP in each layer to zero, so each block starts as identity. Keep all other initializations as in the incumbent. This is a common stabilization for deeper small GPTs at high LR.
backlog.title: Zero-init output projections

backlog.spec: Initialize token embeddings with normal std 1.0 instead of the current default, and keep the EMBEDDING_LR of 0.6 unchanged. Also scale the lm_head initialization down by 0.5 so initial logits stay small. This tests whether a different embedding scale changes early learning.
backlog.title: Embedding init scale

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters with decay 0.999 updated after each optimizer step, and evaluate the EMA weights at the end of training instead of the raw weights. Store the EMA copy in the same dtype. Do not change the evaluation call or the summary printing; only swap the weights before the existing evaluation call.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Start training at half the sequence length used by the incumbent and switch to the full sequence length at 50% of the time budget, keeping the same tokens per step by adjusting the batch dimension. Rotary embeddings and masks must handle the change. This speeds early steps and ends at full context.
backlog.title: Sequence length curriculum

backlog.spec: Add a learned per-channel mix between each token's hidden state and the previous token's hidden state at the input of each block, with mix weight initialized to 0.1 and passed through a sigmoid. This injects a cheap local-context signal before attention. Keep the rest of the model unchanged.
backlog.title: Untied token shift mixing

backlog.spec: In the Muon update step, scale each 2D weight's orthogonalized update by max(1, rows/cols)**0.5, where rows and cols are that matrix's output and input dimensions, so tall matrices (such as the MLP up-projection) take proportionally larger steps. Leave MATRIX_LR at 0.04 for the first run. Apply the scale only inside the Muon step; Adam-optimized parameters are unchanged. Keep the code to one or two lines in the Muon update.
backlog.title: Shape-aware Muon update scaling

backlog.spec: Set the number of key/value heads to n_head // 2 while keeping n_head and HEAD_DIM unchanged. Repeat each K and V head across its paired query heads before attention (for example with repeat_interleave), so the attention call and its shapes stay the same. Keep all other hyperparameters fixed. The goal is fewer K/V projection parameters and cheaper attention, which gives more optimizer steps within the 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Grouped-query attention with half the KV heads

backlog.spec: Replace the ReLU-squared MLP with a gated SwiGLU block: a gate projection and an up projection from model_dim to hidden, then silu(gate) * up, then a down projection back to model_dim. Set hidden to roughly 2/3 of the current MLP width (about 8/3 * model_dim) so the total parameter count matches the baseline. Keep the same Muon and Adam parameter grouping, with all three matrices in the Muon group.
backlog.title: SwiGLU MLP at matched parameter count

backlog.spec: Apply rotary position embedding only to the first half of each head's dimensions. Leave the second half unrotated so it can carry position-independent content. In the attention forward pass, split q and k into rotary and pass-through parts, apply RoPE to the rotary part only, then concatenate back. Keep the RoPE base and all other settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Partial rotary embedding on half the head dimensions

backlog.spec: Scale MATRIX_LR per transformer block with a linear multiplier from 0.6 at the first block to 1.0 at the last block. Build the Muon parameter groups so each block's matrices get their own lr value, computed as MATRIX_LR * multiplier for that layer index. Embeddings, lm_head, and scalar parameters keep their current learning rates. This tests whether early layers need a gentler update than late layers.
backlog.title: Layer-wise learning rate multiplier for matrices

backlog.spec: Keep the linear warmdown for Muon matrix parameters as it is now, which starts at WARMDOWN_RATIO of the budget. For the Adam groups (embeddings, lm_head, and scalars), start a faster linear warmdown earlier, at 0.3 of the time budget, so those groups reach zero LR before the matrices do. Compute each group's LR multiplier from elapsed time fraction separately, and keep the final LR fraction at zero for all groups.
backlog.title: Separate warmdown fraction per optimizer group

backlog.spec: Speed up the training step without changing the math. Set torch.compile to mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs' or an equivalent option that the installed PyTorch supports, and make sure the Muon Newton-Schulz loop and the attention call are inside the compiled region. Use fused AdamW where it is available for the Adam groups. Do not change any hyperparameters or the evaluation code. The goal is a higher step count within the same 300 s, so the change should be a pure speed change.
backlog.title: Compile speed pass for more steps in the fixed budget

backlog.spec: Apply label smoothing with epsilon 0.01 to the training cross-entropy loss only, using the standard target mixing with a uniform distribution over the vocabulary. Keep evaluation loss computed exactly as the harness does, with no smoothing. This tests a small regularizer that may reduce overconfidence on a 300 s run that is far from overfitting, so keep epsilon small.
backlog.title: Light label smoothing on the cross-entropy

backlog.spec: At initialization, multiply the standard init of the attention output projection and the MLP down projection by 1/sqrt(2*DEPTH). This keeps the variance of the residual stream roughly constant as depth grows. Do not zero-initialize these weights. Leave the embedding init, the lm_head init, and all learning rates unchanged.
backlog.title: Depth-scaled initialization of residual branches

backlog.spec: Add a second embedding table of size about 4096 buckets, indexed by a hash of the previous token id and the current token id (for example (prev * 1000003 + cur) % 4096). Add its output, scaled by a learned scalar initialized to zero, to the token embedding before the first block. The table is trained with the Adam embedding group. Compute the hash in torch on the device, so no data pipeline changes are needed. This is a cheap way to add local bigram statistics to the input.
backlog.title: Hashed bigram embedding added to the input

backlog.spec: Add a second token-indexed embedding table (vocab x kv_dim, zero-initialized) in GPT. In every other attention layer (e.g. layers 1, 3, 5, ...), add a gated copy of that embedding lookup to the value projection output before attention: v = v + lambda_l * ve(idx), with lambda_l a per-layer learnable scalar initialized to 0 and a learnable gate. Give this table the EMBEDDING_LR group (Adam) so the extra parameters train with the existing embedding recipe. No change to the forward signature used by evaluation; the lookup uses the same idx tensor already passed to forward.
backlog.title: Value embeddings injected into attention values

backlog.spec: Inside each transformer block, apply an extra RMSNorm (no learnable affine, or a learnable per-channel gain initialized to 1) to the output of the attention branch and to the output of the MLP branch before they are added to the residual stream. Keep the existing pre-norms unchanged. Initialize any new gain to 1 so the block starts near the incumbent behavior. Only the block's forward needs editing; the residual add order stays the same.
backlog.title: Post-sublayer RMSNorm on attention and MLP outputs

backlog.spec: After QK RMS-normalization and rotary embedding, multiply each head's q by a learnable per-head scalar gain g_h initialized to the value that gives the current effective scale (e.g. sqrt of head_dim-based factor used by the attention call), so the model can sharpen or soften attention per head. Store g_h as a parameter of shape (n_head,) in the scalar/Adam group with SCALAR_LR and no weight decay. Keep the attention call and the sliding window arguments unchanged.
backlog.title: Learnable per-head attention logit gain

backlog.spec: Keep the same number of physical transformer blocks but run the middle two blocks twice in the forward pass (weight sharing across the loop), so effective depth grows by two layers with no extra parameters. Apply a learnable per-iteration scalar on the residual contribution of the second pass initialized to 1. Make sure the per-layer window pattern and the per-layer scalar lists are indexed by effective layer, not physical block, so shapes stay consistent. Compute cost rises about 25 percent, so reduce nothing else; the fixed time budget will absorb the cost.
backlog.title: Looped middle block with shared weights

backlog.spec: Initialize the unembedding (lm_head) as a copy of the token embedding weights at startup, then keep them as separate parameters trained with their own groups (EMBEDDING_LR for the input table and UNEMBEDDING_LR for lm_head). Add a single learnable scalar logit_scale (init 1.0, Adam with SCALAR_LR) that multiplies the final logits before the loss. This tests whether a tied-style initialization and a learned output temperature help a small vocabulary model. Keep the loss and evaluation call unchanged.
backlog.title: Untied embedding and output with learned logit scale

backlog.spec: Add one extra prediction head that predicts the token two steps ahead from the final hidden state (shift targets by 2, shared lm_head weights with a separate small linear adapter of shape model_dim x model_dim, zero-initialized). Training loss is the standard next-token cross-entropy plus 0.1 times the t+2 cross-entropy, computed on the valid positions only. The primary logits used for the reported model output remain the t+1 head only, so evaluation is unaffected. Drop the auxiliary term at the start of the warmdown so the final objective matches the metric.
backlog.title: Auxiliary multi-token prediction head

backlog.spec: During the final 30 percent of the time budget, every 50 optimizer steps copy the current raw model parameters into a running uniform average (keep a CPU or GPU fp32 buffer of the same shapes). When training ends, load the averaged parameters into the model before the harness evaluation call, without changing that call or the summary printing. This is distinct from an exponential moving average: it averages a small set of late checkpoints taken while the learning rate is already small, so it should not lag behind the schedule. Skip averaging if fewer than 3 snapshots were taken.
backlog.title: Stochastic weight averaging over the late warmdown

backlog.spec: Keep the micro-batch size fixed at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE, but increase the number of accumulation micro-steps so the effective tokens per optimizer step double once elapsed time passes 70 percent of the budget (for example from 2**19 to 2**20 tokens). Scale the learning rates for Adam and Muon groups by sqrt(2) at that switch point so the larger batch does not stall progress, and recompute the gradient accumulation divisor accordingly. The switch is a single step-based condition on elapsed time; no change to data loading or evaluation.
backlog.title: Late-phase batch growth by gradient accumulation

backlog.spec: Before training, estimate unigram token frequencies from the first few training batches (or a fixed number of steps' worth of target tokens collected in the first 2 percent of the budget) and compute per-token weights w_v proportional to 1/sqrt(freq_v), normalized so the mean weight over observed tokens is 1. Multiply each position's cross-entropy by w[target] before averaging. Do not change which tokens are scored by the evaluation; this only changes the training objective, which pushes capacity toward rare byte patterns that dominate bits per byte on the validation split.
backlog.title: Inverse-frequency token loss reweighting

backlog.spec: Route the token embedding weight (and optionally the lm_head weight) through the Muon update path instead of Adam: treat its 2D shape as a matrix, apply the existing Newton-Schulz orthogonalization to the momentum-averaged gradient, and scale the step by the same shape-based factor used for other matrices. Use a learning rate on the order of MATRIX_LR times 0.5 and keep decoupled weight decay at WEIGHT_DECAY. Leave the scalar and bias groups on Adam. This is a bold optimizer change; if the update diverges, the run should be reported as a loss-based failure rather than tuned further.
backlog.title: Newton-Schulz orthogonalized updates for the embedding table

memo:
Incumbent mean_adjusted is 1.1145 over 16 runs. No change has been accepted yet, but four official scores were lower than the incumbent and were still rejected: the sequence length curriculum (slot 12) at 1.1109 (-0.0036), the logging fix (slot 14) at 1.1126 (-0.0019), the sqrt warmdown (slot 8) at 1.1130 (-0.0015), and one more near that range. These are probably within noise, so replicate the best ones before drawing conclusions. Try combining the sequence length curriculum with the sqrt warmdown.

Did not help: larger or more complex architecture changes. Ten layers was +0.0213, HEAD_DIM 64 was +0.0116, first-layer value mixing was +0.0073, GQA was +0.0015, and cosine decay was +0.0038. The EMA run scored 2.4356, which points to a bug.

Process: of the 20 slots, 4 were patch failures, 3 were aborts, 2 were crashes and 1 was a target_leak invalid run. Copy SEARCH text exactly, keep losses shape-safe, and do not touch evaluation code.
